https://www.dw.com/en/search-resumes-for.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JGBi It's unclear how many of the sailors have survived the shipwreck Image: Alexander Stein/JOKER/picture alliance Advertisement A search-and-rescue operation was continuing on Sunday after a cargo ship sank off the eastern coast of India . The Panama -flagged vessel Ocean Winner had 24 crew on board when it sank on Friday. Two Chinese nationals were rescued on Saturday, with 22 people still unaccounted for, the Indian Coast Guard said. The two rescued Chinese seafarers said the vessel developed a list on Friday and ​sank within eight minutes, forcing crew to abandon ship, said Shyam Jagannathan, ​director general of India's Maritime Administration. 'Developing a list' is a technical maritime term which means the vessel began tilting. The cause for this was not immediately known. Search on for missing crew members The chances of finding survivors fell sharply after 12 hours, but rescuers were continuing the search, Jagannathan ​said. The missing crew members include 18 ‌Chinese ​nationals, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi, according to the Indian Coast Guard. In a post on X, it said it had deployed three ships to conduct surface searches for the remaining crew members. According to officials cited in the Indian Express , the ship was about 240 nautical miles (444 kilometers, 276 miles) off the coast of Odisha. According to ship-tracking app MarineTraffic, the Ocean Winner was carrying iron ore from Paradip port in Odisha to Singapore . Don't let the algorithm hide the news. Photograph: Jay Kogler/AAP Melbourne Woman allegedly repeatedly stabbed with scissors while protecting son from ‘random’ Melbourne CBD attack Man arrested after being restrained and pinned down by ‘heroic’ bystanders, Victoria police say Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Achol Arok Tue 25 Aug 2026 05.01 EDT Last modified on Tue 25 Aug 2026 05.12 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A mother has been taken to hospital after allegedly being repeatedly stabbed by a stranger while protecting her 10-year-old son during a “random attack” in Melbourne’s CBD. The alleged attacker, 27, was arrested at the scene after he was restrained and pinned down by three bystanders, according to Victoria police. The 30-year-old mother was walking along Spencer Street on Tuesday afternoon with her three children when the man allegedly “randomly punched” the child then continued to walk away. Police alleged the man then turned around, grabbed the mother in a headlock and stabbed her repeatedly with a pair of scissors in the back and left shoulder. The incident took place just outside the Melbourne West police station, allowing officers to attend the scene “within a minute”. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Police Supt Zorka Dunstan, who was one of the responding officers, said she was “horrified” by the attack. “I was in my office upstairs, saw what was happening, I came down. One of the boys, he’s an 11-year-old, he was crying … absolutely impacted by what he saw. I gave him a hug because I was impacted just watching how he reacted,” she said. The mother was taken to the Royal Melbourne hospital with non-life-threatening injuries and was in a stable condition. Police said her 10-year-old son was also taken to hospital “as a precaution”. The other two children were not injured. Police confirmed the man was known to authorities in New South Wales and Western Australia with a history of family violence and assault charges. He was not on bail at the time of the alleged attack. Police said there was “nothing to suggest there was any motivation” behind the incident and suspected it may have occurred during a mental health episode. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion The alleged attacker has been deemed “not fit for interview yet” and will remain in police custody ahead of questioning. Dunstan described the actions of the bystanders as “heroic”. She told media she had said to the 10-year-old boy “how lucky that we had such good people intervene and help his mum”. “Any offending of this nature is horrific anywhere, so not just outside the police station, anywhere in the city or outside the city,” she said. “Without a doubt, without their intervention, it could have been a lot worse. So, we are so grateful for their assistance, and I’m sure the family are as well.” Explore more on these topics Melbourne Victoria news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

https://www.delfi.lt/en/politics/judge-o.text: Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.08.13 17:40 Judge orders MP Skvernelis to continue wearing ankle monitor Translated by Karolis Broga Source: Elta EN Judge orders MP Skvernelis to continue wearing ankle monitor PHOTO: Julius Kalinskas | Elta Follow Delfi on Google The court has rejected the appeal of MP Saulius Skvernelis, former leader of the party Democrats For Lithuania, who will have to continue wearing an ankle monitor amid a corruption investigation. On Thursday, 13 August, the Vilnius Regional Court considered Skvernelis’ complaint regarding the decision of the District Court of Vilnius City, which had extended intensive supervision measures for two months, from 2 August until 2 October. Mindaugas Povilanskas, chairman of the Criminal Case Division at the Vilnius Regional Court, noted that Skvernelis, who is a suspect in a corruption case, had numerous times violated more lenient supervision measures by contacting another suspect in the case. Therefore, the judge ruled that tighter supervision measures were applied and extended lawfully. The decision is final and not subject to appeal. Earlier, Skvernelis challenged the requirement for him to wear the electronic tag, claiming that it was hindering his job as a member of parliament. As reported, investigating corruption at the State Plant Service, law enforcement carried out searches at the home and parliamentary office of MP Skvernelis. In April, allegations of bribery were made against the politician, former parliament speaker, prime minister, interior minister and police commissioner general. In December 2025, 13 individuals were detained over the large-scale corruption at the State Plant Service under the Ministry of Agriculture. Later, the number of suspects rose to 15. Investigators suspect that officials demanded bribes from companies transporting plants and plant products in exchange for phytosanitary certificates. More than 100 searches in December uncovered over EUR 1.3 million in cash, about 8 kg of gold valued EUR 1 million, 11,000 packs of cigarettes, 14,000 litres of alcoholic beverages, cocaine and explosives. Among suspects are former State Plant Service head Jurijus Kornijenko and other officials, along with business figures accused of bribery and influence peddling in an organised group. The probe has also implicated politicians. Authorities searched the homes and parliamentary offices of former prime minister and Seimas speaker Saulius Skvernelis and ex-lawmaker Kazys Starkevičius, the latter resigned in March. Starkevičius later admitted to the news website 15min.lt to have taken a EUR 20,000 bribe. Source Topics It is forbidden to copy the text of this publication without a written permission from ELTA. Click for next article What horrors await you in the town of Jeziorne-Kolonia (Image credit: Team17) Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Bluesky Threads Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter In addition to a plethora of new AAA Xbox games revealed at Gamescom 2026, there were just as many indie titles unveiled, aiming to innovate the medium in ways never seen before in terms of gameplay and artistry. One such indie title that caught my eye was a survival horror game called Holstin , which is set to launch in 2027 for Xbox Series X | S , Xbox on PC , Xbox Cloud Gaming , and Xbox Game Pass (Day One) , with Xbox Play Anywhere support, along with PC via Steam and GOG , Nintendo Switch , and PlayStation 5 . Holstin also has a free playable demo available right now on its Steam page . Holstin – Gamescom 2026 Trailer - YouTube Watch On In this game, you have come to a small eastern Polish town called Jeziorne-Kolonia in search of your missing friend Bartek, whose trail was last seen there. Unfortunately, Jeziorne-Kolonia has been possessed by a demonic force that is turning the buildings into pus-filled flesh and its inhabitants into disgusting, mindless abominations that attack anything in sight. You may like A viral co-op horror game is coming to Xbox, Game Pass, and Play Anywhere soon 10 Summer Game Fest indies coming to Xbox you won't want to miss Our favorite horror game of 2025 is back with an upcoming DLC expansion To survive, you will need to scavenge for supplies, solve mind-bending puzzles, seek information from the few sane locals left in the town, and find guns to defend yourself with before the horrors of this town eat you alive. What makes Holstin stand out from the crowd is its 1990s Polish setting, an absolutely gorgeous and grim pixel art style that seamlessly blends 2D and 3D graphics, and most of all, the ability to change top-down and third-person perspectives during gameplay. DEAL: Get Surfshark VPN 86% OFF with Windows Central 🦈 Resident Evil 9 sort of tried this with the alternating first-person and third-person perspectives, but Holstin takes it a step further by letting the player switch perspectives at the push of a button instead of having to fiddle around with in-game menus. This creates a dynamic system where one moment you will be exploring decrepit city streets from a top-down perspective, switch to a third-person perspective to shoot guns at monsters, then flip back to the top-down perspective so you can have a better view of where to safely dodge an attack without getting stuck in the environment. (Image credit: Team17) I'm not normally a fan of survival horror games, as I suck at ammo and medkit conservation, but Holstin has me intrigued with its sublime pixel-art design, grotesque creatures, and interesting gameplay mechanics. If you enjoy scaring yourself on the go with retro-style horror games with Xbox Play Anywhere like the critically-acclaimed Signalis, you will want to keep an eye out for this title when it drops in 2027, as it could be a potential ID@Xbox sleeper hit. Or you could find out now for yourself if it's up your dark alley by its demo on Steam. https://english.news.cn/20261008/c8b1471.text: 1 dead, 2 injured in knife attack at Polish school Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-10-08 18:42:01 WARSAW, Oct. 8 (Xinhua) -- One person was killed and two others were injured in a knife attack at a school near Wyszkow in Poland's central Mazowieckie province on Thursday, local media reported. The attack occurred Thursday morning when a 15-year-old boy entered the school and stabbed the school principal, a cleaner and a teacher, the Polish broadcaster Polsat News reported The 37-year-old cleaner later died despite resuscitation efforts, said the report, adding that the suspect was detained by police. The attack came a day after a 19-year-old student injured nine people in a knife attack at a school in Ostroleka, also in Mazowieckie province. Police arrested the suspect later that day. ■
